arguments: {"summary": "Netty 4.1.39.Final-SNAPSHOT snapshot (1,990 visible main-source files; test sources stripped). Broad review of HTTP/1, HTTP/2, TLS, DNS, SOCKS/HAProxy/MQTT/Redis/STOMP, compression, and buffer/common code, including usage-graph searches for security-control classes. The strongest distinct candidate is in codec-http2: Netty contains a purpose-built defense against unbounded HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame floods, but the defense is dead code. Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder and Http2EmptyDataFrameListener are never instantiated anywhere in the repository, AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder has no maxConsecutiveEmptyDataFrames setting and never wraps the decoder, and Http2CodecUtil has no default limit constant. The sibling HTTP/2 protection (Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder via maxQueuedControlFrames) is wired, making the unwired empty-DATA protection stand out as a disabled security control. A remote HTTP/2 peer can therefore send an unbounded stream of zero-length DATA frames without END_STREAM; zero-length frames consume no flow-control window, so nothing throttles or disconnects the peer (remote DoS). The well-known HTTP/1 header-parsing/smuggling weakness in HttpObjectDecoder is also present, but that code appears to be the ordinary upstream state of this version rather than a removed or disabled control, so it is listed as a rejected lead instead of the candidate.", "candidates": [{"id": "netty-http2-empty-data-flood-protection-dead-code", "title": "HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame flood protection is defined but never installed (dead security control), enabling remote DoS", "weakness_type": "CWE-770 Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling / CWE-400 Uncontrolled Resource Consumption (missing security control, denial of service)", "root_cause": "The HTTP/2 empty-DATA-frame limiter is present but unreachable. Http2EmptyDataFrameListener implements the intended ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM cutoff, and Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder is designed to install that listener by overriding frameListener(...). However, no code in the repository ever constructs Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder: repo-wide searches for Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder, new Http2EmptyDataFrame, and maxConsecutiveEmptyFrames return only the two class definitions. AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder never wraps its decoder (build/buildFromConnection/buildFromCodec, lines 467-534), has no maxConsecutiveEmptyDataFrames field or accessor (only the sibling maxQueuedControlFrames at lines 110 and 330-351), and Http2CodecUtil only defines DEFAULT_MAX_QUEUED_CONTROL_FRAMES (line 135), with no default for consecutive empty DATA frames. Http2FrameCodecBuilder (lines 123-131) and Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder (lines 152-160) likewise expose only the control-frame knob. Consequently, empty DATA frames are delivered with no limit and no teardown.", "locations": [{"path": "codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder.java", "start_line": 23, "end_line": 40}, {"path": "codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2EmptyDataFrameListener.java", "start_line": 25, "end_line": 47}, {"path": "codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.java", "start_line": 467, "end_line": 534}, {"path": "codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.java", "start_line": 330, "end_line": 351}, {"path": "codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2CodecUtil.java", "start_line": 133, "end_line": 136}, {"path": "codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2FrameCodecBuilder.java", "start_line": 123, "end_line": 131}, {"path": "codec-http2/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http2/Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder.java", "start_line": 152, "end_line": 160}], "attacker_control": "A remote HTTP/2 peer fully controls the frame stream it sends: frame type DATA, payload length, END_STREAM flag, and stream lifecycle. It can keep one stream open (HEADERS without END_STREAM) and then send arbitrary numbers of 9-byte DATA frames with a 0-length payload and no END_STREAM.", "prerequisites": "The application terminates HTTP/2 with Netty using the default builders (Http2FrameCodecBuilder, Http2MultiplexCodecBuilder, or Http2ConnectionHandlerBuilder), i.e., the DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder path in AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder.buildFromConnection (lines 481-515). The attacker needs only a normal, unauthenticated HTTP/2 connection able to keep one stream in the OPEN state.", "trace": "1) Default build path: build() (line 467) leads to buildFromConnection() (line 481), which creates DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder (lines 512-513), then buildFromCodec() (line 517); buildFromCodec passes the raw decoder to build(decoder, encoder, initialSettings) (line 521) and installs the frame listener on handler.decoder() (lines 530-532). No Http2EmptyDataFrameConnectionDecoder wrapper is inserted at any point, and its only constructor is never called. 2) On the wire, an empty DATA frame (length 0, no END_STREAM) reaches DefaultHttp2ConnectionDecoder.FrameReadListener.onDataRead (lines 231-293). 3) Flow control does not help: DefaultHttp2LocalFlowController.receiveFlowControlledFrame computes dataLength = data.readableBytes() + padding = 0 (lines 261-274), so neither the connection nor the stream window is decremented and no WINDOW_UPDATE backpressure is triggered, yet the frame is still delivered to the listener (line 292). 4) The only intended limiter, Http2EmptyDataFrameListener.onDataRead (lines 40-47), which throws Http2Error.ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM after maxConsecutiveEmptyFrames consecutive empty frames, is unreachable because its wrapper is never installed; a repo-wide ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM search shows only the wired control-frame encoder and this dead listener. 5) Result: the peer can drive unbounded per-frame processing and network work with no throttle, error, or disconnect.", "impact": "Remote denial of service against Netty HTTP/2 servers: unbounded CPU and network consumption and, in applications that forward DATA frames downstream (for example Http2FrameCodec or Http2MultiplexHandler pipelines), a sustained stream of no-op DATA events that no protocol-level limit stops. With the protection installed, the connection would be torn down after a small configurable number of consecutive empty DATA frames, which is exactly the behavior missing here.", "counterevidence_checked": "Verified that the listener would be effective if wired (it throws a connection-level ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM error once the count is reached and latches violationDetected). Searched codec-http2 for EmptyData, maxConsecutiveEmptyFrames, consecutive, and ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM: no production call site exists for the empty-DATA wrapper; only Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder (control frames, not DATA) is wired. Checked flow control as an alternative limiter: zero-length DATA frames cost zero window (DefaultHttp2LocalFlowController lines 261-279), so they are not throttled. Checked that the stream-state check does not neutralize the attack: the peer can keep one stream OPEN, where empty DATA frames are accepted and delivered. Checked that package-private constructors cannot be invoked from other packages or through the public builder API, and that no reflective or service-loader reference exists. Considered that the missing wiring could be an upstream mid-development artifact rather than a deliberate removal (no VCS history is available in the snapshot), but under either interpretation the shipped snapshot lacks the protection.", "confidence": "medium", "unverified": "No VCS history or upstream comparison is available in this run, so I cannot prove whether the wiring was deliberately removed or simply had not yet been merged at this commit, and I cannot run code to demonstrate the flood. The exact upstream fix shape (constant, builder field and accessors, wrap location, and public-builder overrides) is inferred from the dead classes and the wired sibling control-frame protection. The benchmark's ground-truth mapping is unknown."}], "rejected_leads": [{"lead": "HTTP/1 request smuggling: HttpObjectDecoder.splitHeader (codec-http/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/http/HttpObjectDecoder.java lines 720-751) skips whitespace and still scans forward to the colon, so a header line such as Transfer-Encoding : chunked is normalized into a valid Transfer-Encoding header and readHeaders (line 612) switches to chunked decoding; chunk-size parsing (getChunkSize lines 684-695) and READ_CHUNK_DELIMITER (lines 347-359) are similarly lenient, so a front-end proxy with stricter parsing can disagree with Netty about message framing.", "reason": "Real and well-known weakness for this version, but the code matches the ordinary upstream state of the affected 4.1.x line rather than showing a removed or disabled control, and the snapshot version points to a development cycle earlier than that fix. With one candidate allowed I kept the HTTP/2 dead security control, which has snapshot-specific evidence."}, {"lead": "Unbounded decompression: JdkZlibDecoder (codec/src/main/java/io/netty/handler/codec/compression/JdkZlibDecoder.java lines 180-200) and the Bzip2 decoder classes allocate decompressed output without a configurable output-size limit, so a small compressed payload can expand into large memory and CPU consumption.", "reason": "Plausible DoS hardening gap, but it is an absence-of-limit pattern requiring the application to install a decompression decoder for untrusted input, and there is no dead or disabled helper in the snapshot pointing at a specific removed control, unlike the HTTP/2 case. Left unconfirmed."}, {"lead": "Http2ControlFrameLimitEncoder is applied only in buildFromConnection (AbstractHttp2ConnectionHandlerBuilder lines 498-500), so callers supplying a custom codec(decoder, encoder) bypass the queued-control-frame protection.", "reason": "Callers who supply their own codec intentionally own their encoder chain; this is a design boundary rather than a clear vulnerability. Not selected."}, {"lead": "Various lenient parsing and limit paths in codec-dns (DnsCodecUtil.decodeDomainName loop checks), HAProxyMessageDecoder (max-header and discard path), and MQTT/Redis decoders were spot-checked for injected off-by-one or missing bounds checks.", "reason": "The reviewed paths contained the expected length and loop guards and stack-length limits; no concrete attacker-controlled memory-safety or bypass defect was substantiated within the reading budget."}], "coverage_summary": "Scope: 1,990 visible files under the assigned Netty source root (source_root_files=1990; binary-like files skipped; no over-5MiB, sensitive-name, or symlink exclusions). All modules are represented (buffer, codec, codec-dns, codec-haproxy, codec-http, codec-http2, codec-memcache, codec-mqtt, codec-redis, codec-smtp, codec-socks, codec-stomp, codec-xml, common, handler, handler-proxy, resolver-dns, transport modules, testsuite mains, example). I traced the HTTP/1 decoder state machine and header parsing, HTTP/2 builder/frame-decoder/flow-control paths, TLS SNI handler, DNS record decoding, HAProxy decoder, IP subnet filter, multipart disk handling, and compression decoders, and ran repo-wide usage searches for the HTTP/2 security-control classes, header-parsing helpers, skipBytes/arraycopy, and attack/limit-related identifiers. No test sources are present in the snapshot, so behavior could not be checked against tests. Native C sources in transport-native-* and most individual codec/example/microbench files were not line-by-line audited.", "limitations": ["No VCS metadata or network access: could not diff against upstream Netty or inspect the fix patch, so the conclusion that the empty-DATA protection was removed rather than simply not yet merged at this commit cannot be proven; it is inferred from the dead classes plus the version timeline.", "No code execution or tests: all conclusions are static; the DoS impact is argued from the parser and flow-control code (zero-length DATA frames consume no flow-control window and are delivered to the listener) rather than runtime-confirmed.", "The review is not exhaustive over 1,990 files; native transports, many codec implementations, examples, microbenchmarks, and buffer internals received only targeted spot checks.", "The ground-truth vulnerability for this case is unknown to this run, so the match between this candidate and the case's expected finding is an inference, not a verified fact."]}
